title: StepFun ships Step 5 Preview — 600B MoE, 1M context, weights coming Oct 15
subtitle: The Shanghai lab opened API access on September 20 to a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 27B active parameters and a one-million-token context — priced at roughly a third of the frontier US labs.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: StepFun officially launched Step 5 Preview on September 20 — a sparse mixture-of-experts model with roughly 600 billion total parameters, 27 billion active per token, and a one-million-token context window. API access and StepFun Studio opened the same day, at $1.00 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens. The company said full open weights will publish on October 15 under a permissive license, and independent scorer Artificial Analysis placed the model at 44 on its Intelligence Index — clustered with mid-tier frontier models from the US labs.

The release matters because of what it does to the price-per-intelligence curve. At $1 per million input tokens, Step 5 Preview undercuts GPT-5.5 by roughly two-thirds at comparable quality tiers, and the 1M-token context targets the exact workloads — long-horizon coding, financial analysis, professional knowledge work — where the US labs have been charging premium rates. Sparse MoE with 27B active is also compute-efficient at inference, which is how a Chinese lab operating under export controls can serve frontier-tier context lengths without frontier-tier GPU counts.

This is the fourth major Chinese frontier release of September, following Shanghai AI Lab's Atria Dawn Preview, Zhipu's GLM-5.3 FlashX and Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash. The pattern is now consistent: Chinese labs are matching or exceeding the mid-tier of US frontier capability, opening weights rather than hoarding them, and pricing aggressively. StepFun's IPO has moved from October to November 2026 at a targeted ~$2 trillion valuation — a number that only makes sense if the market believes this pricing pressure holds.

Takeaway for learners — the ceiling of AI capability still sets the headlines, but the floor sets the economics. A 600B open-weight model at $1 per million input tokens means a small team or a school district can now run frontier-class inference on rented GPUs at costs that were impossible six months ago. When you evaluate a tool this year, don't just ask what the best closed model can do — ask what the cheapest open one can do for your specific task, and how much of your workflow that unlocks.
